title: Arrests and Trials
notes: Disposal of persons arrested under the IPC crimes by Police

12.3.1 The crime head-wise details on the disposal of arrested persons are presented in Table-71. During the year, a total of 32,77,186 persons were either under custody or on bail for 23,04,478 various IPC offences under investigation by Police. These also include persons in whose cases the investigations remained pending at the end of year 1997. Out of the total persons who were under arrest, Police could lay chargesheets in 76.3 per cent; 5.0 per cent persons arrested were either released or freed by Police before trial; 18.7 per cent persons remained under custody or on bail at the end of the year as Police investigation could not be completed in their cases. The highest pendency percentage in the disposal of arrested persons was recorded in cases of `Counterfeiting' (58.0%) followed by `Dacoity' (40.0%) and the lowest was observed in `Sexual Harassment' (5.7%). In Chargesheeting of arrested persons, police could establish the charge with as high as 93.5 per cent result in `Sexual Harassment', followed by `Molestation' (85.6%). The lowest level of charge-sheeting in disposing arrested persons was witnessed in cases of `Counterfeiting' (35.9%) as compared to national average of 76.3% for all IPC crimes.

12.3.2 Table-72 presents State & UT-wise disposal of arrested persons under IPC crimes by Police. Bihar State was responsible for 26.4 per cent pendency in the country followed by Tamil Nadu (10.8%), West Bengal (10.4%) and Andhra Pradesh (9.8%). The above 4 States accounted for 57.4 per cent of the total arrested persons in the country whose disposal was pending at the hands of police during 1998.
